merger_description:
Black Kite Partners Pty Ltd (**Black Kite**), HarbourVest Global Private Solution SICAV S.A. (**HarbourVest**) and MA Financial Group Limited (**MA Financial**) are private capital investors (together, the **Acquirers**).

DR2 Holdings Pty Ltd (**DR2**) is the holding company of businesses primarily involved in the supply of telehealth and face-to-face consultations. Its bulk-billed after-hours consultations are completed through approved medical deputising services, National Home Doctor Service Pty Ltd (trading as 13Sick) and Doctorsquare Pty Ltd (trading as DoctorDoctor). Its in-hours (daytime) consultations are completed through 24-7Medcare and are either bulk-billed or privately paid. DR2 also conducts a surgical assistant placement service through Australia Surgical Assisting.

The Acquisition consists of two parts:

* HoldCo acquisition: related entities of Black Kite, HarbourVest, MA Financial and some current management shareholders of DR2 will acquire interests in Galileo HoldCo Pty Ltd (**HoldCo**)
* DR2 acquisition: Galileo BidCo Pty Ltd (**BidCo**), a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo, will acquire 100% of the share capital in DR2.

Together, the Acquisition involves:

* related entities of Black Kite and HarbourVest acquiring new interests in DR2
* MA Financial rolling over its existing interest in DR2, and transferring its interest in DR2 to another related entity and MA-managed fund
* some individual shareholders rolling over their existing interest in DR2
* other existing investors in DR2 exiting their interests in DR2.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition. In particular:
a. there is a small horizontal overlap between parties in the
supply of telehealth services in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of telehealth services in
Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning vertical
or conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary
conduct, bundling or tying of telehealth services in Australia
post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
